proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, 2^n is congruent to 2^(n mod 8) modulo 17.

argument.text: There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^3 > 10.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, 2*n is at least n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^2 is at least n.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, if n mod 8 = 0 then 2^(n) mod 17 = 1.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 32, 2^(n+8) mod 17 is congruent to 2^(n) mod 17 modulo 17.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^2 is congruent to (n^2) + 299 modulo 23.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 345 modulo 5.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^2 > 20.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-4)*(n^3) equals (n-4)*((n^3) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 8 = 0; n mod 8 = 1; n mod 8 = 2; n mod 8 = 3; n mod 8 = 4; n mod 8 = 5; n mod 8 = 6; n mod 8 = 7.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
The steps above establish the statement up to 40, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 40.
